questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+2y+6z=5 \\  & y-10z=-11 \\  & 4x+8y+13z=9\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 4 & 8 & 13 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 4 & 8 & 13 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 0 & 0 & -11 & -11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{11}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+2y+z=-4 \\  & 2x+5y+3z=-10 \\  & 3x+6y+4z=-12\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 2 & 5 & 3 & -10 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 & -12\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 2 & 5 & 3 & -10 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+2z=-3 \\  & x+2y+2z=2 \\  & 3x+4y+4z=8\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and hence solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 4 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & 4 & 4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 17\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+2z=-3 \\  & y=5 \\  & z=-6\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. Substituting both $y=5$ and $z=-6$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+5+2(-6)=-3\,⟹\,x-7=-3\,⟹\,x=4.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=4,$ $y=5,$ and $z=-6.$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}5 & 20 & -10 & -5 \\ -2 & -8 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 20 & -10 & -5 \\ -2 & -8 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & -8 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $\frac{1}{3}$ and the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{2}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & -3x+6y-3z=18 \\  & -4x+8y-3z=2 \\  & y-4z=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & -3 & 18 \\ -4 & 8 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & -3 & 18 \\ -4 & 8 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -6 \\ -4 & 8 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -22 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -22 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -22\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y+z=-6 \\ y-4z=-3 \\ z=-22,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=-22$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-4(-22)=-3\,⟹\,y=-91.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-91$ and $z=-22$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-2(-91)+(-22)=-6\,⟹\,x=-166.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-166$, $y=-91$, and $z=-22.$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+2y-z=4 \\  & -3x-6y+4z=-8 \\  & 3x+7y-z=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ -3 & -6 & 4 & -8 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ -3 & -6 & 4 & -8 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y-z=4 \\ y+2z=-2 \\ z=4,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=4$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+2(4)=-2\,⟹\,y=-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-10$ and $z=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2(-10)-(4)=4\,⟹\,x=28.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=28$, $y=-10$, and $z=4.$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-y+2z=8 \\  & -2x+2y-3z=-11 \\  & x+z=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+2z=8 \\ y-z=1 \\ z=5,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=5$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(5)=1\,⟹\,y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=6$ and $z=5$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(6)+2(5)=8\,⟹\,x=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=4$, $y=6$, and $z=5.$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y-2z=3 \\ y+5z=-8 \\ z=4,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=4$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+5(4)=-8\,⟹\,y=-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-28$ and $z=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+(-28)-2(4)=3\,⟹\,x=39.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=39$, $y=-28$, and $z=4.$ Or, in vector form $⟨39,-28,4⟩.$

canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y+z=1 \\ y+z=-2 \\ -x+2y+z=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y+z=1 \\ y+z=-2 \\ z=2,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=2$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+(2)=-2\,⟹\,y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=-4$ and $z=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(-4)+(2)=1\,⟹\,x=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-5,$ $y=-4,$ and $z=2.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -5,-4,2 \rangle.$

canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=-2 \\  & x+y+2z=-1 \\  & x+2y+z=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get $a_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\begin{aligned}x+y+z=-2 \\ y=3 \\ z=1,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=1$ tells us the value of $z,$ and the second equation $y=3$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting these values into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+(3)+(1)=-2\,⟹\,x=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-6,$ $y=3,$ and $z=1.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -6,3,1 \rangle.$
